principles: Make operator-visible guidance come from the same state that gates already consume.
Fail closed on merge and dirty-file hazards while printing exact safe next steps.
Keep dryRun inspect-only and prove that boundary mechanically.
Preserve reviewer and host evidence separation; guidance must not become self-attestation.
drivers: User confusion came from repeated done_prepare runs and silent or late closure context.
The current story scope is UX/drivability, not changing DONE gate semantics.
Regression proof must be focused enough to run during normal story closure.

options.name: Inline done_prepare preflight and rerun summary with focused smoke
pros: Smallest scoped change because the existing command already owns merge, refresh, validate, and clean-tree reporting.
Lets the smoke exercise the real user-facing transcript without adding a new orchestration surface.
Keeps gate criteria and evidence writers unchanged.
cons: Requires careful helper extraction to avoid making done_prepare.ts harder to read.

options.name: Add a separate preflight command before done_prepare
pros: Cleaner isolation of hazard detection from done_prepare execution.
Could be reused by other DONE commands later.
cons: Adds a second command users must remember and does not solve repeated done_prepare confusion in the command they actually run.

options.name: Only document the workflow without command changes
pros: No behavior change to CLI output.
cons: Does not fix the runtime drivability bug because agents still discover hazards one failure at a time.

chosen: Inline done_prepare preflight and rerun summary with focused smoke
rationale: Chosen because the failure is in the done_prepare operator experience itself. The best fix is to surface hazards, rerun reasons, and generated-file ownership in the command users already run, while proving dryRun remains side-effect free and leaving all gate and evidence writer semantics untouched. The separate-command and docs-only alternatives are excluded because they would preserve the confusing path that caused the incident.

preMortem.scenario: Guidance accidentally suggests committing unrelated dirty files.
preMortem.trigger: dirty-tree reporting groups generated metadata and unrelated user edits together.
preMortem.consequence: An agent may commit another story or user change while trying to close DONE.
preMortem.mitigation: Classify current-run generated files separately from pre-existing or unrelated dirty rows and cover the transcript in the focused smoke.

preMortem.scenario: dryRun mutates lifecycle metadata or process events while reporting planned actions.
preMortem.trigger: new helper reuses the normal write path before checking dryRun.
preMortem.consequence: A read-only diagnostic command changes gate-participating state and invalidates evidence freshness expectations.
preMortem.mitigation: Snapshot git status and story metadata before and after dryRun in the smoke and fail if bytes or status change.

preMortem.scenario: Preflight blocks legitimate same-story generated metadata that done_prepare is allowed to report.
preMortem.trigger: the hazard classifier treats all .lattice story files as unrelated dirty files.
preMortem.consequence: The command regresses the existing metadata auto-closeout path and forces manual guessing again.
preMortem.mitigation: Test same-story generated metadata as a distinct guidance class while unrelated story metadata remains blocked.

preMortem.scenario: Rerun delta output implies review or host evidence can be auto-rebound.
preMortem.trigger: message text says refresh or rebind without naming the legal writer boundary.
preMortem.consequence: Agent may self-attest evidence that should come from reviewer or host lanes.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep rerun guidance to reasons and legal next actions, and assert it does not contain self-attestation language.
